RHETORIC.Definition: the skill of using language to persuade or influence people

PROPAGANDA.Definition: one-sided or false information spread to make people support a political group

TWISTED.Definition: changed so that the meaning becomes false or misleading

CONCISE.Definition: clear and using no more words than are needed

ARTICULATE.Definition: able to express ideas clearly and well

METAPHOR.Definition: a phrase that describes something by calling it something else

SIMILE.Definition: a phrase that compares one thing to another using "like" or "as"

IN PRINT.Definition: in books, newspapers or other printed writing

PENULTIMATE.Definition: second from the end; next to last

JARGON.Definition: special words used by a particular group that others find hard to understand

METAPHORS.Definition: phrases that describe something by calling it something else

SHOW OFF.Definition: try to impress people with what you know or can do

EVALUATED.Definition: judged carefully to decide how good they are

TEMPTATION.Definition: a strong wish to do something, often something you should not do

RECAP.Definition: go over the main points again briefly

STARTING FROM SCRATCH.Definition: beginning from nothing, with no earlier knowledge or work

SMILING DOWN ON YOU.Definition: looking at you with approval, as if from heaven
